A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same FIA research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FIA experiments on object, explicit-content, and artistic-style unlearning, including ablations, adversarial evaluations, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds sampling-budget sensitivity, SDXL evaluations, and comparative computational measurements.

M1.justification: The contrastive saliency formula, temporal aggregation, spatial selection, and concept-agnostic mask fusion remain unchanged. The SDXL evaluation documents no procedural adaptation; added explanations and sample-count disclosures do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Imagenette and its extended ImageNet classes, I2P, five artists, MS COCO-30K, and the same three adversarial benchmarks. SDXL and sampling-budget experiments change model configurations and sample counts within retained task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 20 adds efficiency comparisons against FMN, AC, SPM, ESD, CP, MACE, and UCE, whereas v1's computational table measured FIA alone. The new SDXL comparison uses UCE. Comparator membership in retained accuracy and robustness experiments is unchanged; newly cited methods such as SCULPT are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation on the substantially different SDXL architecture for object and explicit-content unlearning, plus controlled sampling-budget experiments using K = 1, 3, 5, 10, and 20 across three tasks. These substantially extend the evaluation settings. The retained SD1.x protocols are not explicitly revised.

E4.justification: New Appendix D and Table 16 test sensitivity to the number of samples used to estimate contrastive saliency across all three tasks. Existing pruning-target, granularity, concept-agnostic-ratio, scaling, and adversarial analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: The standard deviations already reported in v1 Tables 18–20 remain in v2 Tables 21–23. Seed disclosures are retained, with no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance procedures. The new sampling-budget experiment concerns saliency estimation rather than repeated evaluation runs.

E6.justification: All original table values and graphical results are retained, but substantial new results appear in Tables 16, 17, and 20. On SDXL, FIA reports 3.20% object forgetting accuracy versus UCE's 12.62%, and 38 explicit-content detections versus 243. Sampling-sensitivity and comparative cost results are also added; these are additional evaluations, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–9 are retained. The added signal-propagation discussion in Section 3.1 provides conceptual motivation, without a new derivation, formal assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free multi-concept unlearning through sparse neuron masks, preservation of concept-agnostic neurons, and strong performance below 0.3% overall sparsity. Added experiments do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds a signal-flow interpretation of saliency, infers robustness to prompt wording from the sampling study, discusses SDXL compatibility limitations of baselines, and interprets computational tradeoffs. The limitation concerning image-quality degradation when forgetting hundreds of concepts remains.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 reports availability and provides a repository link. v2 also discloses saliency sample counts, but Section 3.1 specifies K = 50 while Section 4.1 and Table 16 specify 10. Existing hardware, prompt templates, pruning settings, and baseline repository references are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for SCULPT, Stereo, ScaPre, and SPEED, together with pruning and other related references supporting the saliency discussion. The single-concept versus multi-concept organization and FIA's central novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental discussion are condensed and polished while retaining the core narrative sequence. An Impact Statement replaces the Ethics Statement, standalone reproducibility and LLM-use statements are removed, and appendices are reorganized around the added studies.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format, with widespread resizing and repositioning of displays. Three new tables are added and existing appendix tables are redistributed. Figure content remains unchanged, although enlarged Figure 7 overlaps the page-number area.

improvement.justification: The SDXL evaluation and sampling-budget ablation address previously untested transfer and estimation-sensitivity questions, while the reported code location improves reproducibility information. These benefits are limited by conflicting sample counts and unexplained computational measurements: Table 19 gives 11.28 seconds and 2954 MB for one concept, whereas Table 20 gives 0.024 GPU hours and 6.94 GB. The added validation supports a modest net improvement, but these inconsistencies weaken its practical reproducibility.
